doc.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025

title: Classical clarinet, Debussy and a return to his first teacher
summary: He finds classical music daunting but is taking lessons again with his first teacher and eyeing Debussy's First Rhapsody.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: So I have an idea for your shows. I think you should introduce the Mozart Clarinet Concerto and see how that goes over.
Oh, you know classical music for me is something that’s scary.

There’s something about — and I’ve done a little bit, not much, but there are so many good classical clarinet players out there that do it really, really well. And I don’t know there’s something in classical music that I’m not getting or I just feel like there’s so many people that can do it so much better than I could. Just let them do their thing and I can play to my strengths. But I don’t know it’s funny you should mention that because I just hooked back up with my first clarinet teacher. And I had a lesson with him last month and I’m going to have another one with him next month. And since he is such a master at classical music too and theory and reading, he’s able to help me in a lot of areas that I haven’t — I’m pretty rusty at. So just for my own curiosity he is taking me through some of the classical pieces. And one of them I want to work with him on is the Debussy “First Rhapsody” and that’s a really challenging piece. And Benny did a great recording of it in 1940. I don’t know if I’ll ever have the guts to do it on stage. Maybe. I don’t know. But you know I’m noticing in the last few weeks I’ve been looking at it, it has opened my ears to different things. Who knows? Maybe it’ll spark a new creativity in me. I don’t know. But yeah, I don’t know classical music is something else. You’ve really got to have your ducks in a row to do it properly.
And we get so used to taking liberties with our music. We’re making it up a lot of times so it really takes a different kind of concentration I think, to stick to the page.
